sentences.text: Revenue compounded from $6.91 billion in FY2017 [F1] to $216 billion in FY2026 [F10], a 46.6% CAGR [F211].
The path was a step change rather than a smooth climb: revenue was flat at 0.2% growth in FY2023 [D284], then rose 125.9% in FY2024 [D338] and 114.2% in FY2025 [D393].
The FY2024 jump came from Data Center revenue, which grew 216.7% to $47.5 billion [S54][D615], with Data Center up 217% in the filing's own words [P23].
The FY2023 trough in operating margin, down 21.6pp [D299], reflected $2.17 billion of inventory provisions on excess Ampere Gaming and Data Center supply [P35][P38].
FY2026 revenue grew 65.5% [D448], which the filing attributes to data center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI [P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue [D620], up from 19.9% in FY2018 [D598]; I use this share alone because product members in the FY2026 disaggregation overlap and cannot be summed [R2].
Data Center contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% FY2026 revenue growth [D622][D448].
Data Center computing grew 59% on demand for Blackwell, and networking grew 142% on NVLink compute fabric for GB200 and GB300 systems plus Ethernet and InfiniBand growth [P8][D628][D635].
One direct customer was 22% of FY2026 revenue and another was 14%, both primarily in Compute & Networking [P6].
Operating income grew 60.1% in FY2026 [D449] against revenue growth of 65.5% [D448], with an incremental operating margin of 57.3% [D475], so leverage was slightly negative this year.
Diluted share counts step up 303.7% in FY2022 [D251] and 894.5% in FY2025 [D415], a basis break, so I do not compare the 7.4% diluted EPS CAGR [F216] with the 60.8% net income CAGR [F214].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 [F50] sits above the window median of 32.8% [D813] and below the 62.4% high [D812], with a low of 15.7% [D811].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1% [D462][F30], below the 75.0% high [D818].
The FY2026 operating-margin change of -2.0pp [D463] was cost of revenue at -3.9pp [D477], partly offset by R&D at +1.3pp [D478] and SG&A at +0.6pp [D479].
The filing cites a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase obligation charge in Compute & Networking segment profit [P7], but the cited passages do not tie it to the gross margin decline.
The FY2023 bridge of -21.6pp [D299] was cost of revenue -8.0pp [D312], R&D -7.6pp [D313], SG&A -1.0pp [D314] and an unexplained residual of -5.0pp [D315].
The effective tax rate rose to 15.1% [D434] from 13.3% [D379] on a lower share of tax benefits from stock-based compensation, FDDEI and research credits [P2].
Other income of $11.1 billion [X120] lifted net margin to 55.6% [F70], and the filing attributes the change to unrealized gains on equity securities including the Intel investment [P3].

Operating cash flow of $103 billion [F100] was 0.86x net income [D435], and free cash flow of $96.7 billion [F110] was 0.81x [D436], the low of the FY2022 to FY2026 window [D826] against a median of 0.83x [D828].
Free cash flow margin of 44.8% [D432] is close to its window median of 44.4% [D822].
Capex of 2.8% of revenue [D431] is light, but at 2.13x depreciation and amortization [D437] it is well above the 0.71x of FY2024 [D327].
Receivables grew 66.8% [D473] and inventory 112.3% [D474] against revenue growth of 65.5% [D448], and the cited filings do not explain the FY2026 working-capital build.
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion in FY2026 [D441] from $34.7 billion [D386], as cash and investments dropped to $10.6 billion [D439] from $43.2 billion [D384].
This comparison may be a basis break: the pack carries FY2025 short-term investments [X188] but none for FY2026, so I draw no conclusion on the size of the drop.
Investing outflows rose to $52.2 billion [F120], which the filing attributes to higher purchases of equity investment securities and the Groq license agreement [P1].
Net cash was 83rd percentile of six semiconductor peers [D844] against a peer median of -13.9% of revenue [D845], subject to the same data caveat.
Buybacks of $40.1 billion [X150] plus dividends of $974 million [X160] came to $41.1 billion [D443], or 42.5% of free cash flow [D444].
The diluted share count fell 1.2% [D470], and acquisitions cost $1.54 billion [X168].
The current ratio of 3.91x [F190] is below its window median of 4.61x [D831], and return on average equity of 101.5% [D447] compares with a peer median of 20.3% [D849].
Customer concentration: one direct customer was 22% of FY2026 revenue and another 14% [P6].
Two buyers, at 22% and 14% of revenue [P6], make the earnings stream dependent on a few capital budgets.
China (including Hong Kong) revenue fell 21.4% to $19.7 billion in FY2026 [D545][S24], and its share dropped to 9.1% from 19.2% [D544][D541]; the cited passages give no cause.
A market that was a fifth of revenue [D541] is now minor, so growth leans more on the United States at 69.3% of revenue [D503].
Working capital: inventory grew 112.3% [D474] and receivables 66.8% [D473], with days inventory at 125 days [D446] against 113 [D391] a year earlier.
Inventory growing faster than revenue [D448] preceded the FY2023 provisions of $2.17 billion [P35], so it matters if demand slows.
Data quality: overlapping product members [R2], the share-count basis break [D415] and the missing FY2026 short-term investments limit three comparisons above.
I drop the Graphics candidate [R1] because the FY2023 fall of 25% [D754] was followed by 57.0% growth in FY2026 [D747] and Graphics is now 10.4% of revenue [D746].
Gross margin holding at or above 71.1% [F30] would confirm the margin level, while a fall toward the 62.2% window median [D819] would reverse it; both appear in the FY2027 10-K.
Days inventory above 125 days [D446] would confirm the build-up risk, while a return toward 113 days [D391] would ease it, as shown in the FY2027 10-K.
China share rising above 9.1% [D544] would reverse the shrinking exposure, while staying below it would confirm it, per the FY2027 10-K.
Free cash flow to net income below 0.81x [D826] would confirm weakening conversion, while a move to the 0.83x median [D828] or higher would reverse it, per the FY2027 10-K.
